reasons: No tests are visible for this file.
The currency and industry inputs are ignored, so budgets in other currencies are not handled.
A comment asks for this file to stay in step with a scan file that was not reviewed.

terms.meaning: The budget number saved in the data, in US million dollars.
The size of a plant, such as its power rating or output.
Two ways electrical capacity is rated. A plant rated in each can have different megawatt numbers.

depends_on: scan/budgetUnits (named in a comment, not imported here)

sections.name: storedBudgetMillions
sections.title: Reading a stored budget number
sections.what: Turns a stored budget value into a number, or into nothing when the value is empty or not a number. Budgets are in US million dollars.
sections.why: Likely reason: the stored values are already converted, so this only checks they are usable.
sections.watch_out: The industry argument is ignored, so any future per-industry unit rule must be added here and in the scan code the comment names.

sections.name: displayBudget
sections.title: Showing a budget as readable text
sections.what: Shows a budget like $4.2B or $850M, or the placeholder marker when it is missing. Negative values are handled the same way as positive ones.
sections.why: Likely reason: one display format used on every page.
sections.watch_out: The reported currency argument is accepted but never used, so a budget reported in another currency still shows in dollars with no note.

sections.name: displayBudgetRange
sections.title: Showing a low-to-high budget range
sections.what: Shows a range such as $1.2B to $1.5B, or a single value when both ends are the same.
sections.why: Likely reason: some projects report budgets as a span rather than one figure.
sections.watch_out: If one end is missing, that end shows the placeholder marker, which can leave a half-empty range on screen.

sections.name: displayCapacity
sections.title: Showing plant capacity with its unit
sections.what: Shows a plant's capacity with its unit, such as 1,100 MW. If no capacity value is stored it falls back to a plain megawatt figure, or says the capacity is not reported as one value.
sections.why: Likely reason: projects store capacity in different ways, so this picks the best one available.
sections.watch_out: When a unit is missing it shows a placeholder saying the unit is not reported, rather than guessing one.

sections.name: reportedMW, displayAssessment
sections.title: Converting capacity to megawatts and scores
sections.what: Turns a capacity into megawatts for totals: megawatt values stay as they are, gigawatt values are multiplied by 1000, and any other unit counts as zero. Also shows an assessment as a percent, or as Not assessed when it is missing or negative.
sections.why: Likely reason: totals should not add tonnes or other non-power units as if they were megawatts.
sections.watch_out: AC and DC megawatts are not converted to each other, so a total can mix bases, and callers are expected to label that.

summary: Formats project budgets, capacities and assessment scores into the short text shown to users.
purpose: Keeps money, capacity and score displays consistent across pages.
why: Likely reason: budgets are stored in one unit, and the comment on the first function says the figures are converted before they are saved. Shared formatting avoids each page doing it differently.
how: 1. Checks that a stored budget is a real number. 2. Formats it as billions or millions with a dollar sign. 3. Formats a low-to-high range. 4. Formats capacity with its unit. 5. Converts capacity to megawatts for totals. 6. Shows an assessment as a percent or as Not assessed.
inputs: Stored budget numbers, capacity values and unit names, optional currency and industry labels (currently unused), and assessment numbers.
outputs: Short display text such as $4.2B, a placeholder marker when a value is missing, 1,100 MW, and plain megawatt numbers for totals.
risks: Budgets always show in dollars, and the reported currency is accepted but not used, so a budget reported in another currency is shown without any note. Totals mixing AC and DC megawatts are not corrected.
debug: If a budget shows the placeholder marker, check that the stored value is a number. If a budget looks wrong in size, check that the stored value is in US millions. If a capacity shows Not reported as one value, check both capacity fields.
